question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-1,0]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)={x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}-xy+x-y. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[-1,\,1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration. Round the answer for ${x}_{1}$ to **three decimal places**.
$[$ {{field-1}} $-5$ $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $-1$ $]$
$-5$ {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
${x}_{1}≈[$ $-0.510$ $]$
{{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}-xy+x-y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}-xy+x-y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}-y+1 \\ -4xy-x-1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}-y+1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(-4xy-x-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}-y+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(-4xy-x-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6x & -4y-1 \\ -4y-1 & -4x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6x & -4y-1 \\ -4y-1 & -4x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}-y+1 \\ -4xy-x-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6x & -4y-1 \\ -4y-1 & -4x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}-y+1 \\ -4xy-x-1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6(-1) & -4(1)-1 \\ -4(1)-1 & -4(-1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}3(-1)^{2}-2(1)^{2}-1+1 \\ -4(-1)(1)-(-1)-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-6 & -5 \\ -5 & 4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}24/49 \\ -19/49\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{24}{49} \\ -\frac{19}{49}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{24}{49} \\ -\frac{19}{49}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-0.510 \\ 0.612\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
